tools.name: get_damage_rules
tools.description: The rules a host, platform or rental car company has to follow when charging a traveller for damage, for Australia or the US. Returns plain facts, the evidence to ask for, where to escalate and official sources. Use when someone asks whether a damage bill or charge is allowed or fair.

tools.name: check_deadlines
tools.description: Works out the dates that matter for a damage charge: whether an Airbnb host asked in time, when the traveller's reply window closes, and the US credit card dispute deadline. Only uses dates the user gives (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: evidence_to_request
tools.description: The exact documents and photos a traveller should ask the host or rental company for before paying a damage charge.

tools.name: start_bill_check
tools.description: Returns a link that opens neatly's check on the website with the bill type and company already chosen, for when you can't pass the user's files yourself. If you can access the files, use check_bill instead.

tools.name: check_bill
tools.description: Runs neatly's free check on the user's actual damage bill. Send the bill (screenshot, photo or PDF) and/or the damage photos the host or rental company sent, as https links or base64. neatly checks the photos (AI-made or edited, reused, photos of a screen, photo dates) and every charge against the p

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Gets a neatly report by its link or id. Before the full report is unlocked: the verdict, each charge with its number of points and strongest stamp, the dispute estimate and the reply deadline. Once unlocked (paid, or free because the bill was fair): every finding, what the bill charged, the evidence

tools.name: unlock_full_report
tools.description: Starts a one-off payment for the full report and ready-to-send replies. The price depends on the amount the points challenge (US$19 / US$39 / US$59 / US$89 in United States; A$29 / A$59 / A$89 / A$129 in Australia; £15 / £29 / £45 / £69 in United Kingdom; €17 / €35 / €55 / €79 in Ireland; C$25 / C$5

tools.name: payment_status
tools.description: Checks, straight with Stripe, whether the user has paid for the full report and for Round 2 on a report, and what to do next. Call it after the user says they've paid, or any time before offering a purchase so you never offer something they already have.

tools.name: check_their_reply
tools.description: Round 2, free part. Once the full report is unlocked and the host or company has answered, send their reply (pasted text and/or up to 4 screenshots). neatly checks it against every point raised and returns which points they answered, partly answered or ignored, any new amount, and how much new evide

tools.name: unlock_round2
tools.description: Starts a one-off payment for Round 2 after check_their_reply: the notes on each point, the evidence still missing and the next reply ready to send. Returns a secure Stripe checkout link for the user to open and pay themselves. Never ask for card details. After they pay, call get_round2.

tools.name: get_round2
tools.description: Gets the Round 2 result for a report. Before payment: the verdict and the status of each point. After payment: the notes on each point, new evidence, what's still missing, the next reply and the next step.

tools.name: list_companies
tools.description: Lists the hosts, platforms and rental car companies neatly checks bills from in Australia or the US, with a page about each and whether neatly has company-specific facts.

tools.name: check_fee
tools.description: Explains one type of damage-related fee and the law or platform rule that limits it, for Australia or a US state: loss of use, admin fee, processing fee, diminished value, repair estimate instead of an invoice, cleaning, wear and tear, old item charged as new, late damage request, deposit kept. Incl

tools.name: where_to_complain
tools.description: The escalation path for an unfair damage charge with official links: Australian state fair trading offices, the ACCC and AFCA, or in the US the card dispute route, state attorneys general, the FTC and CFPB, plus known company claim contacts.

tools.name: draft_evidence_request
tools.description: Writes a free, polite message asking the host or rental company for the evidence behind a damage charge, ready to paste. A general template: for a reply written around the user's actual bill and findings, run check_bill and the full report.

tools.name: list_guides
tools.description: Lists neatly's guides for Australia or the US: Airbnb's new house rules (from 20 Nov 2026), holiday rental car damage bills, Victoria's bond evidence rules, spotting AI-edited damage photos and fake invoices, disputing Hertz, Thrifty and Sixt damage scanner bills, which rental companies use AI damag

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Returns a whole neatly guide: the answer, every section, FAQs and sources. Use the slug from list_guides.

tools.name: about_neatly
tools.description: What neatly is, how the check works, the six checks, price, guarantee, privacy (photos are not kept), who runs it and the answers to common questions. Use it when the user asks whether neatly is trustworthy, what it costs or what happens to their photos.

tools.name: list_supported_providers
tools.description: The full registry of vacation rental, hotel, rental car, car share, RV, moving truck and deposit or bond brands and jurisdictions neatly audits in Australia or the US: category, parent group, the reply deadline that applies, the charges to check, the evidence to ask for, sourced facts and the brand'

tools.name: get_provider_dispute_rules
tools.description: For one brand (e.g. Budget, Thrifty, Camplify, Alamo): the deadline that applies, the charges most worth checking, the evidence they should provide, sourced facts, and the full report price for a given bill amount.

tools.name: create_audit_session_url
tools.description: Returns a /check link with the brand, amount and currency already filled in, so the user can upload the bill and photos and get the free audit in about two minutes. No account needed.

tools.name: generate_baseline_vault_url
tools.description: Returns a link to Baseline Vault, where the user takes 4 photos at check-in or vehicle pick-up and seals them with a timestamped receipt in about 60 seconds. Photos stay on their phone. Use it before a trip or when the user is arriving or collecting a car.

tools.name: get_report_summary
tools.description: Same as get_report. Kept for older clients.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_audit_session_url, generate_baseline_vault_url · Private data: evidence_to_request, start_bill_check, check_bill, check_their_reply, where_to_complain, generate_baseline_vault_url · Public sink: check_bill, get_report, unlock_full_report, check_their_reply, unlock_round2, list_supported_providers, create_audit_session_url · Destructive: draft_evidence_request.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_audit_session_url, generate_baseline_vault_url · Private data: evidence_to_request, start_bill_check, check_bill, check_their_reply, where_to_complain, generate_baseline_vault_url · Public sink: check_bill, get_report, unlock_full_report, check_their_reply, unlock_round2, list_supported_providers, create_audit_session_url · Destructive: draft_evidence_request

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
